name: India: Kashmir, Manipur and the Maoist belt

status.en: 288 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 17% fewer than the week before, most of them in Delhi, Mumbai and Hyderabad.
status.nb: 288 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 17 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Delhi, Mumbai og Hyderabad.

summary.en: Opposition leaders and journalists marched to the Supreme Court demanding the resignation of the election chief, confronting police barricades and being detained by police. In Azad Kashmir, four men were killed by a landmine explosion near the LoC in the Poonch area. In Manipur, authorities have not performed an autopsy on a Naga man whose missing head is being sought by the state government. The conflict continues in Kashmir, Manipur and the Maoist-affected belt, with 437 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Opposisjonsledere og journalister marsjerte til Høyesterett og krevde at valgkommissæren skulle gå av, de konfronterte politibarrikader og ble arrestert av politiet. I Azad Kashmir ble fire menn drept av en landmineeksplosjon nær LoC i Poonch-området. I Manipur har myndighetene ikke utført obduksjon på en Naga-mann hvis savnede hode blir etterlyst av delstatsregjeringen. Konflikten fortsetter i Kashmir, Manipur og i den maoist-påvirkede beltet, med 437 kamprelaterte dødsfall i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Kashmir conflict
background.extract: The Kashmir conflict is a territorial conflict over the Kashmir region, primarily between India and Pakistan, and also between China and India in the northeastern portion of the region. The conflict started after the partition of India in 1947 as both India and Pakistan claimed the entirety of the former princely state of Jammu and Kashmir. It is a dispute over the region that escalated into three wars between India and Pakistan and several other armed skirmishes. India controls approximately 55% of the land area of the region that includes Jammu, the Kashmir Valley, most of Ladakh, the Siachen Glacier, and 70% of its population; Pakistan controls approximately 30% of the land area that includes Azad Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan; and China controls the remaining 15% of the land area that includes the Aksai Chin region, the mostly uninhabited Trans-Karakoram Tract, and part of the Demchok sector.
